question: Naming was rung 4 because the protocol still stopped. Does dropping the king and decoding at every party reach rung 5 --- the answer comes out anyway?

corrupt_3.refused_past_capacity: more than 2 parties sent wrong shares of a masked product, which is beyond the decoding capacity of a degree-4 sharing over 9 points

too_few_parties.refused_to_start: robust ATLAS needs n >= 4t+1 to correct t wrong shares of a degree-2t product; got n=7, t=2, which corrects only 1

load_caveat: host-a was at load average around 37 of 64 vCPU. Traffic, round counts and correctness do not depend on load; no wall-clock figure is reported here.

rounds.note: for 2000 and 22000 multiplications. Dropping the king removes a round: it was to the king and back, and it is now one all-to-all.

what_this_does_and_does_not_make_robust.robust: the degree-reduction step, which is where a wrong share used to stop the protocol
not_robust: the double sharings, from Shamir<T>::get_randoms --- hyper-invertible matrices with no malicious check in this build. A corrupt contributor can make [r]_t and [r]_2t inconsistent with each other and no decode on either alone sees it.
the inputs, which in QOMM are bound by the dealer's per-share Pedersen commitments and in this benchmark are not
what_this_does_and_does_not_make_robust.why_the_first_one_is_acceptable: it is preprocessing, and preprocessing consumes no inputs --- a failed run leaks nothing and denies nobody an outcome. It is re-run, and a node that keeps failing it is removed between auctions, which is governance rather than protocol.

prediction.8 elements per party for the all-to-all,: WRONG, 1.6x low. Measured 18.222; the swap from king to all-to-all costs 12.889 rather than the modelled 6. The model counted global traffic on the sending side only and the discrepancy has NOT been isolated, so it is a bad model rather than a finding.
prediction.one round per layer against ATLAS's two: LANDED in the form that matters: 8 rounds against the king's 9, and 12 against 13 at the larger size.
prediction.one or two corrupted nodes corrected AND: LANDED, and this is the result. corrupt {0}, {0,1} and {8} all returned the correct answer with the culprits named; {0,1,2} refused past capacity.
prediction.n >= 4T+1 enforced rather than assumed: LANDED: at n=7 the protocol refuses to start rather than running with a capacity of 1 against a threshold of 2.
